title: Recording Remember in the Padded Cell, Chicago
summary: Love Song to a Chambermaid and Remember; the padded Chicago studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: It's interesting, I was at the Institute of Jazz Studies last Friday playing somethings that you had written that I hadn't heard, and I heard some of those things from the Red Norvo period like "Love Song to a Chambermaid".
And things that were a little later, like "Remember".

in June, because I had made arrangements before that, to get ready for that. "Remember" I think was already in the works in the autumn of '36, and recorded in '37; that's true. I remember it well, in Chicago in the Padded Cell.
It was a studio, near the water tower, but it was all thick padding. There was no reverberation of any sort. That's the way they did it in those days. That's why it sounds that way.
